violating.description: The order lookup with get_order is skipped entirely.
The confirmation step with confirm_with_user is skipped.
The confirmation is asked after the refund has already been issued.
A partial refund of 25 is issued instead of the full order total of 40.
The receipt is sent before the refund instead of after it.
The order lookup is moved to after the confirmation, so it no longer happens first (still before the refund).

preserving.description: Same calls in the same order, but serialized as compact JSON on one line without a trailing newline.
Key order is swapped inside each call (args before tool, amount before order_id) with 4-space indentation.
The confirmation message is worded differently but still states the amount and order.
The refund amount is written as 40.0 instead of 40.

violating.description: The combined multiple-of-15 check is dropped, so multiples of 15 return "fizz".
The fizz check uses 9 instead of 3, so most multiples of 3 fall through.
The buzz check uses 10 instead of 5, so odd multiples of 5 fall through.
The fallback returns the string of n + 1, an off-by-one.

preserving.description: Builds the answer by concatenating fizz and buzz parts instead of a separate 15 check.
Checks both-divisible via both modulo tests, reorders branches, uses an f-string, and omits the trailing newline.
Renames the parameter and uses a lookup table keyed by the two divisibility flags.

preserving.description: Counts lines with splitlines and words per line, using a different algorithm and compact separators.

files.solve.py:
import json
from pathlib import Path

text = Path("input.txt").read_text()
rows = text.splitlines()
lines = len(rows)
words = sum(len(row.split()) for row in rows)
Path("stats.json").write_text(json.dumps({"lines": lines, "words": words}, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")

preserving.description: Counts lines with awk and prints with printf, adding a pretty-printed multi-line layout.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
n=$(awk 'END { print NR }' data.txt)
printf '{\n  "status": "ok",\n  "items": %d\n}\n' "$n"
